XPENG demonstrates IRON adapting to changing hand gestures

The research robot follows visual cues without spoken commands; XPENG reports a 0.2-second reasoning-update interval.

Humanoids Daily ↗23 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 2

Following a changing interaction

A new video shows a tester changing from a handshake to a fist bump and high-five. IRON adapts and uses its other arm when the target moves out of reach. XPENG attributes the visual, speech-free interaction to VLA 2.0.

Update frequency is not total latency

XPENG describes continuous observation, planning and movement with reasoning updates every 0.2 seconds, or five times per second. That interval is not total camera-to-motion latency. The demonstration also does not establish that the system is identical to the model in XPENG vehicles.

A demonstration rather than a rollout

The footage is labeled an R&D test version. Attempt counts, success rates and separate prediction-accuracy tests are absent. It demonstrates adaptation to changing gestures, without establishing readiness for general customer use.
